data.name: Bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitors
data.description: Bivalent compounds (e.g. RMC-5552) engaging both an FKBP12-dependent site and the active site, giving deeper mTORC1 inhibition with selectivity over mTORC2.
data.description_beginner: A newer design: deep inhibition of one complex only.

studies.title: The Bi-steric, mTORC1-Selective Inhibitor, RMC-5552, in Advanced Solid Tumors: A Phase 1 Trial
studies.authors: Schram AM; Naqash AR; Haura EB; Riess JW; Ulahannan SV; Ou SI; Munster PN; Cheng ML; Gustafson WC; Bitman B; Friedman R; Penn R; Kar S; Seshadri V; Wang Z; Tao L; Yang YC; Singh M; Burris HA; Meyerowitz JG

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human (Phase 1 dose escalation, n=57, advanced solid tumors, NCT04774952)
studies.finding: First-in-human, open-label dose-escalation trial (n=57, advanced solid tumors, no comparator arm) of a bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor. Treatment-related hyperglycemia was low (4%) and not dose-limiting, alongside a 64% disease control rate. Because the trial was uncontrolled and made no head-to-head comparison against rapamycin or an ATP-site inhibitor, this is encouraging early clinical evidence consistent with the hypothesis that sparing mTORC2 reduces metabolic toxicity -- it does not establish mTORC2 sparing as the cause.

relations.mechanism: A bivalent molecule engages an FKBP12-dependent site and the active site simultaneously, producing deeper mTORC1 inhibition than a rapalog while sparing mTORC2.
relations.boundary: Phase 1 in advanced solid tumours – a safety and pharmacodynamic result, not an efficacy verdict. Directness is graded indirect because, like rapalogs, the mechanism requires FKBP12. Consensus is emerging: one trial, newest evidence in the corpus.
